overview: White develops the bishop modestly to e2, an Inverted Hungarian, rather than to b5 or c4. The usual continuation is 3...Nf6 4.d3 d5 5.Nbd2 (Inverted Hanham) or 4.d4 with a Scotch-like game. White is looking for a solid, slow game and Black has easy equality.

white_ideas.idea: Play d3, O-O and Nbd2 for a solid set-up.
Challenge the centre later with c3 and d4.

black_ideas.idea: Develop and equalise easily, then play on the kingside.

typical_structures.structure: Black e5/d5 centre against a White d3/Be2 set-up (Hanham reversed).

character.notes: Quiet and slow with no forcing lines.

gambit.notes: The Basman Gambit 4.d4 exd4 5.e5 is a rare sub-line.

structure.notes: Centre fluid, with e4 and d3 against Black's e5/d5.

sublines_that_differ.name: Basman Gambit
sublines_that_differ.how: White gives a pawn for quick play against the knight.

character.reason: Quiet development with a sound structure.

gambit.reason: The main line has no material given; the gambit is a rare sub-line.
